chunks: And if any of your women go away to the disbelievers, and you succeed (in gaining spoils), then give to those whose wives have gone away as much as they had spent; and fear Allah, in whom you are believers.

key_terms.مِثْلَ مَا أَنْفَقُوا: as much as they had spent (dowry)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on compensating husbands when their wives migrate to the disbelievers?
ai.summary: This verse, revealed in the context of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, establishes the principle of reciprocal compensation (muqabalah) when spouses separate due to migration during wartime. Shia scholars emphasize that the compensation is limited to the dowry (mahr) rather than the full value of the wife, reflecting a specific legal equity between the migrating woman's family and her husband. It serves as a practical application of divine justice, ensuring that neither party suffers an unjust financial loss due to the political and military shifts of the era.
